analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patch and metadata units. InferenceHandler changes at head lines 135 and 513 replace autopilotAllowsModel with autopilotServesModel in local and final network admission checks. Their security effect cannot be established without the two predicates and residency-transition callers; integration must verify that newly selectable models cannot bypass intended serving/retirement gates or admit work during teardown (TB-002, TB-007, T-010, T-053). The supplied head lines 620–1556 are unchanged surrounding behavior: response encryption fails closed (799–855; T-008), cancellation retains delivered-output billing floors (1361–1433), and terminal attestation commits emitted content/reasoning/tool deltas (1163–1204, 1512–1537). No regression in those paths is supported by the complete change ranges.
MTPUpgrade adds transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) at head line 127 after acquiring the loading flag and before memory claims. BASE lines 122–199 retain identity checks, memory admission, cancellation cleanup and load-gate release; lines 202–259 show idle-only replacement and native retirement. Integration must inspect transitionGenerations and its consumers to confirm that beginning this generation invalidates stale residency/capacity decisions correctly on successful, failed and cancelled preparation. A missing matching end call is not established as a defect: generation semantics are outside this evidence. No supplied change alters cache account scoping, SSD cryptography or donation policy (T-041), Apple authorization, token custody, privileged helper authority or release qualification. No independently supported finding qualifies; remaining uncertainty concerns the changed admission predicates and generation contract, not a claim that missing source is safe.
